papers.title_en: Protein-independent light harvesting governed by structural heterogeneity
papers.authors: Arai, S., Inagaki, T., Harada, J., Azai, C., Kondo, T.
papers.evidence: 使用超快瞬态吸收光谱，一种时间分辨技术
papers.tldr: 绿硫菌的叶绿体天线无蛋白支架，依赖自组装的管状和层状细菌叶绿素聚集体实现高效捕光。通过单分子超快瞬态吸收光谱解析出六个动力学组分，发现层状聚集体趋向激子局域化以扩展捕光能力，管状聚集体维持离域激子并作为主要能量供体。结构异质性作为功能特征，平衡了捕光容量与定向能量传输，揭示了无蛋白支架下的分工机制。
papers.abstract_en: Chlorosomes are the largest known photosynthetic light-harvesting antennas, yet unlike protein-based antennas, they lack protein scaffolds that organize pigment molecules and instead contain self-assembled tubular and lamellar bacteriochlorophyll aggregates. How these antennas achieve directional and efficient energy transfer has remained unresolved. By applying ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy to individual wild-type and mutant chlorosomes, we resolved six kinetic components obscured by ensemble averaging and assigned each to an excitation process associated with either lamellar or tubular aggregates. Lamellar aggregates tend toward exciton localization and expand light-harvesting capacity, whereas tubular aggregates retain a relatively delocalized excitonic character and serve as the primary energy donors to the baseplate. Structural heterogeneity therefore emerges as a functional feature that balances light-harvesting capacity with robust directional energy transfer. These findings reveal a division of labor among self-assembled pigment aggregates for efficient light harvesting without protein scaffolds.
